participants.note: suggested using a shared mutex instead of an atomic counter and extending DEBUG_LOCKORDER for non-LIFO shared lock releases

claims.harm: using an atomic counter for cursor synchronization is non-standard and less suitable than a shared mutex
claims.quote: I'm not sure about this approach with an atomic counter though. Would it make sense to instead have a shared mutex that would allow multiple consumers to take a read lock along with the cursor, which are then released in the destructor?
claims.settled_by_quote: Thanks, took your suggestions, @andrewtoth. I reworked the fix around it

claims.harm: DEBUG_LOCKORDER cannot handle non-LIFO lock releases when long-lived shared locks outlive outer locks
claims.quote: Since we now take a shared lock while inside a separate lock which is released while the shared lock continues to be held, it would require us to make a modification to make sure we're popping the correct lock being released. This would let us catch issues with DEBUG_LOCKORDER.
claims.settled_by_quote: Thanks, I implemented both suggestions and pushed the reworked series.

result.notes: andrewtoth suggested replacing the atomic counter with a shared mutex and updating DEBUG_LOCKORDER for non-LIFO lock releases; l0rinc implemented both suggestions. sedited provided a Concept ACK.
